title: add-benchmark-lab-adaptive-batching-reporting-pipeline-v76
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds adaptive batching profiling harness, representative workload runners, and a reporting pipeline to aggregate profiling baselines and perf metrics. Backwards-compatible change; no user-facing API breakages.
description: Context: The benchmark lab needs repeatable profiling baselines and a reporting pipeline that ingests representative workload runs with adaptive-batching parameters. Motivation: improve regression detection for latency and throughput changes, and enable automated recommendations for batching configs in Redwood Optimize. This PR implements: 1) an adaptive-batching runner that replays representative workloads while sweeping batch size and target latency knobs; 2) a profiling-baselines schema and loader to persist canonical runs; 3) a Dagster reporting pipeline that aggregates run results, computes summary metrics (p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-token), and exports to the perf warehouse; 4) representative workload runner templates and local run scripts; 5) unit and integration tests and CI workflow updates. Checklist: - [x] Implement adaptive-batching runner and parameter sweep - [x] Add baseline schema and migration - [x] Add Dagster pipeline and exporters - [x] Add representative runners and example configs - [x] Add tests and CI job - [x] Docs/README updated - [x] Verified end-to-end on staging Impact: Improves our ability to detect performance regressions on kernel, quantization, and batching changes. The reporting pipeline is additive and runs under a new schedule; it does not change existing results retention. See linked Linear tasks for follow-ups: tuning default sweep ranges and adding visualizations in the Console. How to run locally: python benchmark-lab/runners/adaptive_batching.py --config examples/benchmark-lab/configs/representative_web.json --out results/local_run.json dagster job execute -m benchmark_reporting -a perf_warehouse --env staging Notes: The integration test suite had a transient flake related to Docker image pulling; CI rerun is included in checks. This PR intentionally keeps runner resource defaults conservative to avoid large cluster impact on first rollout. If merged, schedule will be added to nightly pipeline in a follow-up that toggles full-sweep mode.
